internal: an independent review by a Claude subagent, 2026-11-14 (docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-20261114.md), findings IR-H-1, IR-H-2, IR-M-2, IR-M-3, IR-L-2 and IR-L-3, each reproduced before it was counted. Expected: a production panic path on the line of a proved test function (named as a function, and inside a macro's arguments); a panic path in a new file whose first line the grammar reads as a shebang and the compiler as an attribute and an opened comment, so that the cfg(test) under it is comment text; the trivial assertion and the placeholder written over lines inside another macro's body (declared misses, marked syntax_unchecked, until 2026-11-14: the tokens of a hunk are now read across its lines); a conditional skip whose condition changed from miri to all(); unwrap and expect passed as functions or called by a path; a spaced allow attribute. Negatives: an ignore that belongs to a serde attribute; unwrap_or_default passed as a function. Declared false positives: a method named expect on a hand-written parser and on a mock, and a Python name that begins with unittest.skip; and since 2026-11-14 two that were negatives until then: the panic path in the cfg(test) module of a file created whole, read inside a macro's arguments (the parser never removes evidence any more; it is reported with test_likely), and the conditional skip of which only the reason changed (an attribute that starts on an unchanged line is the same as before only if its whole text is, second independent review IR2-M-1, and the reason is part of the text). Declared misses: cfg(any()) on a test; and respellings in Python, JavaScript and Go, where no parser backs the token rules (a skip raised as an exception, assertions with a message, with parentheses or with inner spaces, chained skip modifiers, a spaced call, an empty error check with the operands reversed)

internal: a second independent review by a Claude subagent, 2026-11-14 (docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-2-20261114.md), findings IR2-H-1, IR2-M-1 and IR2-M-2, and round 9 of Vesper's review (docs/reviews/vesper-v3-round9-report-20261114.md), finding VD3R9-M-1, each reproduced before it was counted. Expected: a production panic path in a new file whose first line holds //* inside a block comment, which the grammar does not count as a nested opener and the compiler does, so that the cfg(test) after it is comment text (it was withdrawn as proved test code); unwrap called by a path that is broken after its ::, passed as a function of the patch's own type, named as a value with generic arguments over two lines, and called after a comment that the lexer's code view ends too early; a conditional skip applied by a cfg_attr inside a cfg_attr; a conditional skip whose nested condition changed from all(miri) to all(); a removed test written #[r#test]. Negatives: an import named expect, a path that only leads through a module named unwrap, and a condition of which only the spacing changed. Declared false positive: a panic path in the cfg(test) module of a file created whole, reported with test_likely since the parser never removes evidence. Declared miss: a call inside another macro's body after /* /* */ // */, where the parser names no construct and the lexer's code view, which does not nest block comments, shows the token rules a comment. Changed 2026-11-14, when the parser left the evidence path and the tokens of a hunk are read across its lines (docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-3-20261114.md): a construct over lines is reported on its first added line, the line of the :: and not of the name; two more declared misses, the function of the patch's own type passed as a value (the parser named any path used as a value; tokens do not tell one from an import or a type, and only the standard Result and Option are read) and the call after /* /* */ // */ in plain code (the parser nested the comment; the code view does not); and one more declared false positive, the condition of which only the spacing changed (nothing is compared with the old side any more: a line written again inside a conditional skip is a change to it). Changed again 2026-11-14 (review round 12): the code view reads Rust as the compiler's lexer does and nests block comments, so the two calls after /* /* */ // */ (in plain code, and inside another macro's body) are found; they moved from the declared misses to the expected items. The function of the patch's own type passed as a value stays declared

internal: two findings of the independent reviews of 2026-11-14 against the code view (crates/deep-diff-forge-graph/src/lexical.rs), each reproduced on the released v0.8.3 binary with a control before it was counted, and a third text found while the fix was written. (1) IR2-H-3, docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-2-20261114.md: Rust nests block comments, and the view ended one at the first */, so after /* /* */ a // cut the line and the call behind the last */ was hidden (src/net.rs: a fetch, a spawn, an unwrap, a todo after a nested comment that holds a quote, and an unwrap after a comment that holds //*; v0.8.3 reports no signal for the file, and process_spawn and network_fetch for its control). (2) IR4-H-1, docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-4-20261114.md: a character literal with an escape longer than one character put the view one quote out of step, so that '"' opened a string and "/*" a comment over the rest of the hunk (src/table.rs, a new file whose first line is such a constant: the unsafe block, the unwrap, the todo, the ignored test and the trivial assertion after it; src/escapes.rs, the same with '\u{1F600}'|'"' and a byte literal: v0.8.3 reports no evidence for either file, and unsafe_added for their controls). (3) src/piled.rs: a string and then a raw string that holds a comment opener on each of three lines; a scanner that counts comment depth has one reading for each depth, and the reading that resumed both strings, the compiler's, must not be the one dropped (found by the fuzz oracle against rustc's lexer while the fix was written; released versions read it right). Expected: every item. The fuzz target rust_code_view holds the view to the compiler's lexer for any text

internal: a fifth independent review by a Claude subagent (docs/reviews/claude-independent-review-5-20261114.md, IR5-H-1, IR5-M-1, IR5-M-2) and round 12 of Vesper's review (docs/reviews/vesper-v3-round12-report-20261114.md, VD3R12-M-1, VD3R12-M-2), 2026-11-14, each reproduced before it was counted. Expected: after a string over a line end, an unwrap, a todo, an ignored test and a trivial assertion with the comment /*""*/ between two of their tokens (src/union.rs), a conditional skip with a closing bracket inside a string of its condition (src/skip.rs), and the unwrap in a hunk of an existing file (src/cli.rs): the bytes of two readings were united and the union showed the comment's quotes between the tokens; raw identifiers after the left-to-right mark U+200E, which the compiler takes for white space (src/marks.rs); a spawn on a line added inside an existing block comment, // */ ... /*, and the same with the opener added by an earlier hunk (src/net.rs, src/lib.rs): a side below line 1 is also read as beginning inside a block comment; a spawn under a shebang line that holds /* (src/bin/tool.rs); every item under m!(k#r"\"); m!(" /* "); (src/kraw.rs), which rustc 1.99.1 reads as k, # and a raw string in editions 2015 and 2018 and refuses in 2021 and 2024; and the unwrap on the line that closes a string opened above the hunk (src/db.rs, the review's honest case): a side that, read from code, ends inside a string is also read as beginning inside one. Declared false positives, the cost of those two further readings: a call in the text of a string after **/ in a hunk below line 1 (src/glob.rs), and a call in the text of a string in a hunk that ends inside another string (src/log.rs). Declared misses: the spawn, the ignored test and the trivial assertion under m!('r#r"\"); m!(" /* "); (src/rawlt.rs), which editions 2015 and 2018 read as 'r, # and a raw string where 2021 and 2024, which the code view follows, read one raw lifetime and an ordinary string; and a spawn after // "; in a hunk whose string was opened by an earlier hunk (src/store.rs): read from code that side ends in code, so nothing says it began inside a string
